haiku-low.q1: Keys load at startup before ready. /healthz returns 503 until all three keys are in the snapshot, then 200. The server may listen earlier.
haiku-low.q2: It retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero (code 70) and never becomes ready. The rollout halts, old pods keep serving, and customers see nothing.
haiku-low.q3: Every 5 minutes it reads each secret. If the version id changed, it validates the value and swaps in a new snapshot. On failure it keeps the last good value, logs a warning, and retries.
haiku-low.q4: Only in process memory, in the snapshot {name: (value, version_id)}. Never on disk, in env vars, logs, exception messages, chat, tickets or files.
haiku-low.q5: Only the prod service identity orders-api-prod can read prod values, read-only. Only the security on-call can write them, and only they can revoke keys. Engineers have no access.
haiku-low.q6: Old keys remain in git history and in old images, which can be redeployed as rollback. They become harmless only when revoked at the providers, after rollback is blocked and adoption is proven.
haiku-low.q7: Each client calls secrets.get on every request and puts the current key from the snapshot into the Authorization header. There is no store call on the request path.
haiku-low.q8: Evidence gate: every pod's secret_version_in_use shows the new id for all three keys, refresh succeeded after the last store write, no warnings, no old-image pods, and no unexplained old-key traffic.
haiku-low.q9: Set store access (step 7), create new provider keys and load the store (step 8), switch the app and remove yaml keys (step 9, deployed in step 11), then revoke old provider keys last (step 14).
haiku-low.q10: make run sets APP_ENV=dev and reads orders-api/dev/* with the engineer's own identity, getting provider sandbox keys. Offline mode uses fixed dummy keys, not real credentials.
haiku-low.q11: An attempt succeeds only if all three secrets are fetched and non-empty. A partial load counts as a failed attempt, so it retries, then exits non-zero and the pod never becomes ready.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED. The document says security has not decided on a scheduled rotation or its cadence; it is an open question that security owns.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded first. The HTTP server may listen early, but /healthz returns 503 {"status":"starting"} until the snapshot holds all three keys. Then it returns 200 and the instance is ready.
sonnet.q2: It retries after 2 seconds, up to 3 retries (4 attempts, about 6 seconds). Then it logs the error class and exits non-zero (e.g. code 70). The pod restarts and never becomes ready. The rollout halts, the old pods keep serving, and customers see nothing.
sonnet.q3: A timer in each instance fires every 300 seconds and reads each secret. If the version id differs, it checks the new value (non-empty, no stray whitespace), swaps in a new snapshot and logs the refresh. If the read fails, it keeps the last good value, logs a warning with the secret name and error class, and retries at the next tick. The pod stays ready. An alert fires if the last success is older than 15 minutes.
sonnet.q4: They are held in the in-memory snapshot, a map {name: (value, version_id)} that is replaced whole. They must never appear on disk, in env vars, logs, exception messages, chat, tickets or files. Debug logging, error reporting and tracing must not capture request headers either.
sonnet.q5: Read: only the prod service identity orders-api-prod (read-only on orders-api/prod/*). Engineers cannot read prod values. Write: only the security on-call, on orders-api/prod/*.
sonnet.q6: The old values stay in git history, which is not rewritten, and in old images, which are also used for rollback. What makes them harmless is that the old keys are revoked at the providers in step 14, after the new keys are proven in use. The pre-migration images are deleted afterwards.
sonnet.q7: The new snapshot replaces the old one. On each outbound request the client calls secrets.get('<name>'), takes the current key from the snapshot and puts it in the Authorization header. No key is copied at import and there is no store call on the request path.
sonnet.q8: Evidence, not elapsed time. Every running pod shows the new version id for all three keys in secret_version_in_use. Every pod's last refresh success is newer than the last store write. No pod reports a refresh warning. No old-image pod exists anywhere. The provider dashboard shows no unexplained recent traffic on the old key after a quiet period of at least 24 hours or as the on-call decides.
sonnet.q9: 1. Confirm assumptions and inventory (step 6). 2. Set up store access and encryption (step 7). 3. Create new keys at the providers and copy them into the store (step 8). 4. Build the app change that reads from the store and removes keys from the committed file, in one PR with the CI guard (step 9). 5. Staging soak, prod rolling deploy and refresh proof (steps 10-12). 6. Block rollback and handle other consumers (step 13). 7. Revoke the old keys last (step 14). Rotation is split: new keys are created first and old ones revoked last. Removing keys from the file happens in the same change as switching the app, not as a separate step.
sonnet.q10: With make run, APP_ENV=dev. The app loads config/app.yaml plus config/app.dev.yaml and reads sandbox keys from orders-api/dev/* using the engineer's own identity. Alternatively APP_ENV=dev-offline uses local mock providers with fixed dummy keys.
sonnet.q11: An attempt succeeds only if all three are fetched and non-empty. So it counts as a failed attempt and is retried after 2 seconds, up to 4 attempts. Then it exits non-zero and never becomes ready, and /healthz stays 503.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. It is an open question: security has not decided whether or how often, and no cadence is chosen.
